value.name: Charlene and Alice confront Dicky
value.description: Charlene and Alice accuse Dicky of taking credit and being a junkie, escalating the argument in the gym.
evidence: CHARLENE You got the focus and confidence from O'Keefe and Sal and your father and me!
ALICE You were lucky to win that fight, Dicky saved him!
CHARLENE We saved him! Dickya junkbag!

value.name: Dicky asserts sobriety
value.description: Dicky angrily defends himself by saying he has been sober for eight months.
evidence: DICKY Fuck you, Charlene, I'm 8 months sober.

value.name: Charlene taunts Dicky about his back
value.description: Charlene mocks Dicky by implying he will need drugs for his back now that he is out.
evidence: CHARLENE I'm sure you'll need somethin' for your back now that you're out.

value.name: Dicky demands equal treatment
value.description: Dicky argues that if O'Keefe can be present despite his own problems, Dicky should be allowed in because he is family.
evidence: O'Keefe's in the same boat I am, one day at a time, why's it all right for him to be here, but not me? I'm blood.

value.name: Micky rejects outside interference
value.description: Micky insists that he is the one fighting and that he alone knows what he needs.
evidence: MICKY I'm the one fighting, not you, not you, and not YOU. I know what I need.

value.name: Charlene questions Micky's need for Dicky
value.description: Charlene challenges Micky by asking whether he really needs Dicky involved.
evidence: CHARLENE (GETS SHRILL) And you need Dicky?

value.name: Micky chooses family support
value.description: After the confrontation, Micky decides he wants Dicky, Charlene, O'Keefe, and his family around him.
evidence: Micky roils as he makes this decision.
MICKY I want Dicky back. And I want you, Charlene, and I want O'Keefe, and my family.
